findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector shield in the ice machine was observed with accumulating mold slime during the inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure that it is cleaned. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are clean so that Ready-To-Eat foods are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during this inspection did not have a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) completed and available. They were instructed to have enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda gun in the bar area was observed with mold growth in the holes and around the inner rim of the nozzle. The bar manager was shown and education conducted. This item counts as a food contact surface and needs to be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) regularly to prevent pathogenic growth from accumulating. The item was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

A gallon of milk in the walk in cooler was observed partially consumed and without a date marking. When asked the PIC indicated that it was opened a couple days prior. Education was conducted and a date marking added to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are correctly date marked at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) If used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

The blade of the can opener was observed soiled during this inspection. Staff indicated that the item had not been used yet today, indicating that it was left soiled overnight (or longer). The PIC was shown and moved the can opener to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact equipment are cleaned regularly throughout the day (at least every four hours).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Two moist wiping cloths are observed on different surfaces. Education was conducted and the cloths moved to their sani buckets to correct. Ensure that all wiping rags are stored between uses in the relevant sanitizer of sufficient concentration.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result. 

An employee was observed to be eating a bowl of soup on the prep line as the inspector arrived. The PIC halted the consumption and discarded the bowl prior to inspector intervention. Ensure that consuming of foods in the facility does not pose a concern of contaminating foods and/or food contact surfaces in the facility.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

Mold is observed on cheese in a container in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and discarded the container during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all foods remain free from spoilage in the facility.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw fish is stored over cooked pasta in the prep cooler to the west of the prep line. Education was conducted with the PIC and the containers moved to correct. Ensure that staff knows how to store foods in the coolers to prevent possible cross contamination in the facility.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During this inspection there was not a CFPM available in the facility. The current PIC only has a food handler card. The PIC was instructed to acquire a CFPM prior to the next routine inspection to be complaint with the code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen is not readily accessible for use. When discussed the PIC stated that the middle sink of the three part sink is primarily used for this purpose currently. Re-arranging of the area was discussed so that the sink intended for hand washing is useable by staff at all times. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained readily accessible at all times to promote good hand washing practices. The triple sink method is currently being allowed until the adjustment can be made to the kitchen space and because all items needed for hand washing are observed in the vicinity of the sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11. 

On arrival the dish machine would not register sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. The machine was primed several times and eventually reached the needed concentration for safe food contact sanitizing. Ensure that all sanitizers in the facility are at effective levels at all times.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11(D) Reheating for Hot Holding. (D) Reheating for hot holding as specified under (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 5C (41F) and the temperatures specified under (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours. 

Multiple items are observed in the steam table at the beginning of this inspection and are being reheated at this time. This set up is not sufficient for re-heating the items within two hours in the current configuration. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the items moved to the flat top for rapid reheating to correct. Ensure that all parts of Ready to Eat foods are reheated to 165F within two hours.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

1) An opened gallon of milk is observed without a date marking in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was shown and discarded it during the inspection to correct. 2) A container of sticky rice is without date marking in the walk in cooler. The items was asked about and stated that it was prepared last Saturday, making today day 7. The PIC was reminded that this item needs to be used or discarded by the end of today. A date marking was added to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all Ready to Eat Time/Temperature Control for Safety foods bare a date marking if they remain at the facility 24 hours after preparation/opening.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sani bucket available in the kitchen area. Preparation of several foods has begun prior to inspector arrival. A sani bucket was provided during this inspection to correct. Sanitizers need to be available for use at all times that foods and food contact items are being handled.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the employees currently at the facility do not have signed reporting agreements or other similar paperwork available. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they looked for the form given out by this department. Blank copies of the form were found and copies made. The currently available employees signed copies during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all food handlers in the facility have been notified in a verifiable manner their responsibility to report foodborne illness related symptoms and diagnosis.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen had a table in front of it making it difficult for convenient use. The PIC moved the table to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained readily accessible at all times to promote good hand washing practices.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sani bucket available in the kitchen area. The PIC was asked for one and immediately made a bucket using a CL solution. Ensure that sanitizers are available at all times that foods are being handled/prepared.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

A soda is observed in a cup on the shelf over a prep cooler in the kitchen. Education was conducted with the PIC and the cup removed to correct. Ensure that employee drinks are stored so that contamination of consumer foods are not a concern.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved. 

The ice scoop in the bin in the bar area is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This would provide for bare hand contact of ice (a Ready-To-Eat food). Ensure that scoop is stored in a manner to protect the RTE foods in the facility. The scoop was moved during this inspection to correct the violation. Education was conducted with the PIC and the bartender.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

1) The two sani buckets in the kitchen are observed extremely low on both inspector and facility test strips. The buckets were remade to correct. 2) The bar three part sink barely registered a color change on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC indicated that two tablets are normally used for this sink. The instructions indicate 1-2 tablets per gallon of water and approximately 2-3 gallons of water are in the sink. Another tablet was added and the solution came out correctly when re-measured. Shifting the SOP to using three tablets is suggested and regular testing is highly suggested.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The PIC/CFPM during this inspection does not currently have an ANSI accredited allergen training certification. All CFPMs at the facility are required to maintain this certification in addition to their managers certification at all times. Ensure that all CFPMs at the facility have completed allergen training prior to the next routine inspection. Maintain a copy of the certification at the facility. Previous hand outs for this are observed in the facility during this inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to begin handling cleaned/sanitized silverware without hand washing. Multiple practices were observed prior to this event including drinking, menu service, order taking, drink service and wiping the hands on their shirt/pants. Ensure that hand washing takes place prior to handling cleaned food contact surfaces. No gloves were used in this process. Education was conducted during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved. 

The ice scoop in the bin in the bar area is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This would provide for bare hand contact of ice (a Ready-To-Eat food). Ensure that scoop is stored in a manner to protect the RTE foods in the facility. The scoop was moved during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The PIC during this inspection does not currently have an ANSI accredited allergen training certification. All CFPMs at the facility are required to maintain this certification in addition to their managers certification ant all times. Ensure that all CFPMs at the facility have completed allergen training prior to the next routine inspection. Maintain a copy of the certification at the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Both sani buckets in the kitchen are observed low during this inspection. One registered 0 on the inspector’s test strips and was heavily soiled while the other just registered low. Both buckets were remade during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

A container of spray glass cleaner is observed with a whipped cream lid on it and stored in the bar reach in cooler alongside other items intended for consumer food service. The PIC was shown and the container removed to correct the violation. Ensure that all non-food safe chemicals are stored separately from items intended for food service.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

PIC during this inspection does not currently have an ANSI accredited allergen training certification. Ensure that all CFPMs at the facility have completed allergen training prior to th next routine inspection. Maintain a copy of the certification at the facility.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

The hand sink off of the bar area is observed with a coffee pot soaking in it as well as with food items in the drain trap. PIC consulted and it was reviewed that hand sinks can only be used for hand washing. Do not use them as a dump sink or for equipment/ utensil cleaning. The sink was cleaned during this inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

A moist rag is observed on the cutting board of the prep cooler next to the hand sink in the kitchen. PIC consulted and the rag moved to a sani bucket to correct. Ensure that the rags are stored in solution between uses moving foreword.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

PIC during this inspection does not currently have an ANSI accredited allergen training certification. Ensure that all CFPMs at the facility have completed allergen training prior to th next routine inspection. Maintain a copy of the certification at the facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Employee reporting agreements were not available at time of inspection.  All employees are required to agree to and sign Employee Reporting Agreement.  Employee Reporting Agreement states any employee experiencing FBI like symptoms to notify PIC to prevent contamination of food.  Ensure employees sign agreements and keep on-site and available for future inspections.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
REPEAT - Employee was observed to shut off water faucet without using a barrier.  Not using a barrier to turn off faucet handles after hands are washed exposes clean hands to contaminates.  Ensure a barrier is used after washing hands.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice machine was observed to contain an accumulation of mold on baffle.  Discussed with PIC, clean regularly to prevent mold accumulation and contamination of ice.  Ensure ice machine baffle is regularly cleaned.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Knives were observed to be stored in between a metal pipe and the wall, where the clean knives were in direct contact with the wall.  Discussed with PIC, who removed and washed knives.  The wall and pipe are not cleaned and sanitized regularly, which causes contamination of clean knives.  Ensure knives are stored in another manner.

4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Utensils were observed to be stored in a bucket containing food debris.  Discussion with PIC revealed utensils were extras not in use.  Discussed discarding or storing utensils in a container with a lid to prevent contamination.  PIC had utensils and bucket washed immediately.  Ensure utensils are cleaned and stored properly.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Hood baffles above fryer and grill were observed to contain an accumulation of grease, food, and dust residue.  Discussed with PIC, baffles shall be cleaned in between service dates to prevent debris build-up.  Ensure baffles are cleaned regularly to prevent food contamination.

Mold accumulation was observed on the caulk along the dish machine and 3 part sink.  Discussed with PIC, clean area and replace caulk.  Ensure areas subject to moisture are cleaned regularly to prevent mold accumulation.

4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of new caulk:
-Along 3 part sink and dish machine.
-Men’s and women’s bathrooms.
-Hand sink near bar

Indoor material shall be smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable.  These areas are all subject to moisture, which accumulates in small, hard to clean areas.  Ensure these areas are re-caulked.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Faucet in 3 part sink was observed to be separated from sink backing.  Physical facilities shall be maintained and in good repair.  Ensure faucet is securely attached to sink backing.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed kitchen staff use bare hands to shut off faucet. Education provided. Ensure when washing hands, a paper towel barrier is used to shut off faucet to avoid recontaminating of hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

Paper towel dispenser is completely blocked by dishes upon inspector arrival. Discussed with PIC. See that hand sink components are completely accessible at all times to facilitate proper hand washing. See that kitchen equipment is stored away from the handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

Upon arrival, inspector observed a cell phone, a open cup of coffee, and a soda can on top of the prep cooler in the kitchen by the handsink. Discussed with PIC. See that all personal items and beverages are stored on a designated space away from food prep surfaces. Staff may also place drinks on the lowest level of a shelf/prep table as long as it will not contaminate equipment if spilled. See that drinks are covered with a lid and a straw.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. 

Bar prep cooler observed holding ambient temperatures of 60 degrees. Majority of items within are alcohol and/or soda, however 3 cans of whipped cream observed within. Items voluntarily discarded by PIC at time of inspection. See that a refrigerator technician is called to service cooler. In the meantime, do not store any TCS beverages/toppings in this cooler.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Upon inspector arrival, no sanitizer bucket is available for use and food preparation was underway. Discussed with PIC. Ensure a bucket is made prior to operating for ease of access/cleanup. COS- bucket of 100 ppm Cl- made.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The following physical facilities need repaired in the kitchen:
-Seal particle board with paint on shelves where clean dishes are kept
-On the same wall where particle board shelves are hung, nudo board is observed coming off the wall. Seal the board back onto the wall to eliminate gap.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

CFMs do not have allergen awareness training completed. See that training is completed, and certificates available, by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

Container of blueberries in the salad prep cooler is molded over. Discussed with PIC. Conduct regular checks of conditions of food, especially during periods of slow service, low hours of operation. Same applies for date marking violation. Container of blueberries discarded.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf).

Various prepared sauces, soft cheese salad toppings, salad dressings observed with dates that exceed the 7 day date mark rule. Discussed with PIC. It appears as if the containers are reused, but old date marks remain in some cases. Ensure fresh date marks are placed on containers and/or trays containing portioned out sauces and dressings. When bulk containers are opened, ensure a date mark is written on the container itself and used/discarded within 7 days (date of prep+6days). At least 6 containers of salad dressings/sauces discarded, freshly prepared sauces according to manager relabeled with fresh labels. 

Note: discussed other past violations at facility, prior to manager starting, where a thaw date was not indicated on items that were pulled from freezer. Ensure staff places a new label of the thaw date of any items that may be pulled from freezer.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. 

Back door by freezers in kitchen appears to have a slight gap in the frame, allowing sunlight to come through. Ensure door is tight sealing, so pests do not have access. Will follow up at next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PIC and any other CFMs must complete an ANSI accredited allergen training program. Information sheet provided at time of inspection. Complete course and print certificate(s) to show at next inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Food employee touched salmon and handled food without washing hands. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed CFPM place on gloves without washing hands first to handle a pan of raw salmon. Corrected on sight. Salmon was discarded due to date-marking issue explained in violation #23.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date of salmon marked on 4/15 exceeds the time limit. Food was discarded. 

Establishment is only open Wednesday and Friday during winter hours. Food is prepared, frozen, and thawed in between service days. CFPM explained salmon marked 4/15 was thawed two days ago. Inspector discussed making a date label showing prep date, frozen date, thaw date, and use by date to ensure the product is only used 7 days in total. Food was discarded at time of inspection.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15  (C) The handsink plumbing needs repair. Repair handsink according to Illinois and local Plumbing code. Reference 5-205.15.

Observed handsink faucet spraying out extremely hot water. Handsink also fills up quickly with water while in use. CFPM keeps a small plunger on sink to alleviate clogging. CFPM stated it was recently repaired by a licensed plumber.
